evidence: commit 610d10c -- Task 20 (F18 closed: Purview label policy published)
commit 7ba45d6 -- Task 25 (F23 closed: three G3 teardown scripts authored, fix round 3)
assertion.rationale: F18 (Task 20): infra/purview/labels.ps1's Initialize-SensitivityLabel created the four-label taxonomy but Invoke-Main never published a policy scoping it to anyone - a label nobody can apply enforces nothing. labels.ps1 now also defines Get-LabelPolicyScope (the four demo groups infra/entra/manifest.json names - mls-flight-operations, mls-security-team, mls-finance, mls-executives) and Initialize-LabelPolicy, wired into Invoke-Main, which publishes the single policy mls-demo-label-policy via New-LabelPolicy and updates it in place on drift (AddLabel/RemoveLabel/AddExchangeLocation/RemoveExchangeLocation) via Set-LabelPolicy - same create-if-absent/update-on-drift shape as Initialize-SensitivityLabel, gated by -WhatIf the same way. The controller's ruling on this task found a THIRD defect of the identical shape inside L04.md itself, beyond the brief's two: L04.md:57-60 claimed the mls-operations auto-label policy was 'applied by the same script where the AIP-P2 entitlement is present (checked at runtime)' - labels.ps1 had no auto-label function and no entitlement check at all, and closing the policy-publish half while leaving that claim standing would have reproduced F18's own defect shape in the very file being fixed. Decision on that third defect: corrected L04.md rather than implementing a runtime check, because the claim was wrong independent of licensing - labels.ps1's only authenticated surface is an S&C PowerShell session, and the cmdlets that apply auto-labeling (New-AutoSensitivityLabelPolicy/Set-AutoSensitivityLabelPolicy) scope only to Exchange/SharePoint/OneDrive/Teams locations, none of which is a Fabric workspace; there is no 'same script' apply path to build regardless of the AIP-P2 entitlement. infra/purview/auto-label-design.md is now authored as a design-only document recording this reasoning and what a real Fabric-native implementation would need. verification/layer-04-audit.ps1 gains a V4.3 criterion (Test-LabelPolicyScope) - read-only (Get-LabelPolicy, the mls-verifier View-Only Configuration role's Get-Label counterpart) - asserting the policy exists with exactly the four labels and exactly the four demo groups; it is supplementary, not a master-plan criterion, so (same convention as CP-9's V6.5) it is documented in L04.md's Validation cycle but not added to docs/runbooks/layers/README.md's 43-row traceability table or .github/README.md's per-script V-range summary, which stays V4.1-V4.2 intentionally. TDD: 9 new/updated assertions in infra/purview/tests/labels.Tests.ps1 (policy publish, idempotent replay, label-drift and scope-drift update-in-place in both directions, -WhatIf no-mutate) and 5 new/updated assertions in verification/tests/layer-04-audit.Tests.ps1 (V4.3 present on an all-pass run, FAIL on missing policy / missing group / extra group / missing label, V4.1 staying independent of a V4.3 failure) all failed against the pre-fix labels.ps1/layer-04-audit.ps1 (mutation-checked: reverted each file to its pre-fix content, confirmed every new test went RED, restored); all pass after the fix. At the time Task 20 closed this control, F18 was checked to be its sole contributor (no other finding in the register cited CM-6) and the control was asserted CLOSED on that basis. F23 (Task 25) is a SECOND, now-also-closed contributor, added to this record rather than left to make the 'sole contributor' sentence above stale: kill-rebuild.md section 7 instructed an operator to run infra/purview/teardown.ps1 (plus infra/entra/teardown.ps1 and infra/policy/teardown.ps1, which map to no control) for G3 full-tenant handback, and none of the three existed. A Purview teardown that hits file-not-found during a real handback leaves the same four labels and their published policy sitting in the tenant indefinitely after the operator has been told they are gone - a second, independent way CM-6's labeling-and-flow-enforcement intent could fail in practice, distinct from F18's 'policy never published in the first place' gap. infra/purview/teardown.ps1 now exists: it removes the published label policy first (a label still scoped by a live policy cannot be deleted), then the four labels, reusing labels.ps1's own Get-Label/Get-LabelPolicy surface plus new Remove-Label/Remove-LabelPolicy calls; gated by -WhatIf, refuses to run under $env:GITHUB_ACTIONS without an explicit -AllowAutomation no workflow ever passes, and treats an already-absent label or policy as a no-op. 15 assertions in infra/purview/tests/teardown.Tests.ps1 cover the CI refusal, the policy-before-labels order, the -WhatIf no-mutate guarantee, and idempotent replay; all failed before the script existed, all pass after; the CI-refusal, order, and -WhatIf behaviours were each mutation-tested individually (neutered one at a time, confirmed the corresponding test alone went red, restored). Both contributors to this control are now closed, so CM-6 stays CLOSED - not because F23 was irrelevant to it, but because closing it left no open finding against it either. Not claimed: infra/purview/teardown.ps1 has never been run against a live Purview session - verified only by the mocked Pester suite, per this branch's constraint against tenant writes.

recommendation: None outstanding for this control. A regression in EITHER contributor would reopen it: the Initialize-LabelPolicy call removed from labels.ps1's Invoke-Main without replacement, V4.3 deleted from verification/layer-04-audit.ps1 without replacement, labels.ps1's Get-LabelPolicyScope silently narrowed to fewer than the four demo groups L04.md names (all F18), or infra/purview/teardown.ps1's policy-before-labels order reversed, its CI refusal removed, or the script deleted without a replacement that still satisfies CLAUDE.md's teardown-triplet rule (F23). If a future contributor builds a real Fabric-native auto-label apply path (infra/purview/auto-label-design.md describes what that needs), that is new scope, not a reopening of this control.
